s: A company will rehost 60 Windows Server VMs that run Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise edition. The company owns Windows Server Datacenter licenses that were purchased in 2018 without Software Assurance, and SQL Server Enterprise core licenses with active Software Assurance. The company must comply with Microsoft licensing terms, must track license usage by physical core, and wants to reuse its existing licenses. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective?
o: Launch the instances as Dedicated Instances with BYOL Windows Server and SQL Server, and track the licenses in AWS License Manager.

Launch the instances on Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts with BYOL images for Windows Server and SQL Server. Use AWS License Manager license configurations and a host resource group to automate host allocation and track core usage.
Launch the instances on default (shared) tenancy with BYOL Windows Server images, and use License Mobility for both Windows Server and SQL Server.
Launch license-included Windows Server with SQL Server Enterprise instances on default tenancy.

w.y: Windows Server licenses without Software Assurance or License Mobility can be brought to AWS only on Dedicated Hosts, and only if they were purchased before October 1, 2019, which these were. Dedicated Hosts expose sockets and physical cores, and AWS License Manager host resource groups automate host allocation and core tracking, so reusing both licenses is the MOST cost-effective compliant option.

o.A: Dedicated Instances do not provide socket or physical-core visibility, so they do not meet Windows Server BYOL terms.
o.B: Correct: compliant BYOL with physical-core visibility and automated tracking.
o.C: Windows Server is not eligible for License Mobility, so BYOL on shared tenancy is noncompliant.
o.D: Compliant, but it pays again for licenses the company already owns, so it is not the most cost-effective.

d: MOST cost-effective; comply with licensing terms; track by physical core
